entry.name: Seed-Start Grant SA
entry.summary: Matched grants for early-stage South Australian businesses commercialising an innovative product or service.
entry.eligibility: Australian-incorporated company with an active ABN; non-tax-exempt and GST-registered; turnover below A$1 million in each of the prior three financial years; based, or willing to be based, in South Australia before the project starts.
entry.limits: Seed grants are A$50,000–A$100,000 at a 2:1 government-to-applicant match. Start grants are A$100,001–A$500,000 at a 1:1 match. Defined commercialisation projects and a unique product or sustainable competitive advantage are required; confirm current round terms.

facts.Geography: Based, or willing to be based, in South Australia

provenance.evidence: The official business.gov.au programme page lists the grant as open, publishes both matched-funding bands and match ratios, and requires an Australian company with ABN and GST registration, turnover below A$1 million in each of the prior three financial years, and a South Australian base or commitment to relocate before project commencement.

entry.name: First Nations Innovation Acceleration Program QLD
entry.value: Investment grants up to A$100,000 plus advisory services
entry.summary: Funding and dedicated business advisory support for established Queensland First Nations businesses developing innovative products or services.
entry.eligibility: A First Nations-owned business that is established and operating in Queensland, developing an innovative product or service, and seeking advisory support and possible funding to accelerate that innovation.
entry.limits: Applications close 4 February 2027, or earlier if fully subscribed. The source describes support for mature, established businesses, so this is a scale-up pathway rather than an idea-stage startup grant.

facts.Eligibility: First Nations-owned, established and operating in Queensland
facts.Closing date: 4 February 2027; may close earlier if fully subscribed

provenance.evidence: The official business.gov.au listing shows the programme open to 4 February 2027, subject to earlier closure if fully subscribed, and specifies Queensland operation, First Nations ownership, an innovative product or service, grants up to A$100,000, and targeted advisory support for mature businesses.
